messages:
nina: Noticed a spike in SSE reconnects on us-east after the proxy keepalive rollout. Clients hit ECONNRESET and immediately reconnect — looks like keepalive TTL is shorter on proxy tier than upstream.
cho: saw that too. Proxy config set tcp_keepalive_time=30s but backend expects 75s. We should never have asymmetric TTLs.
liam: can we mitigate client-side with exponential backoff? Many clients don't backoff so we get thundering reconnects.
nina: quick mitigation: enable proxy side graceful-close that sends a 30s shutdown warning event before closing socket. That gives clients a chance to reconnect more gracefully.
cho: temp fix: change proxy keepalive to 90s to match upstream and roll back the keepalive tuning. I'll open a patch.
liam: console ask: we need per-tenant keepalive mismatch alarm + a small timeline entry that links proxy config change to reconnect spikes. Currently it's hard to correlate.
deploy-bot: patch:proxy/keepalive-rollup v1 deployed to 5% at 14:22 UTC
cho: long-term: add telemetry flags: keepalive_proxy, keepalive_backend, close_reason, reconnect_backoff_hint. Also add a synthetic check in canary that exercises long-lived SSE connections.
liam: also add a rule in rollout UX: if keepalive TTL changed by > 10s, require canary and synthetic long-lived test.
nina: owners: Cho will revert TTL and add telemetry; Liam will add synthetic test and UX rule; I'll file patch and postmortem draft.
cho: ping @security about whether keeping longer keepalive has any abuse implications.
liam: thanks, creating follow-up doc with exact telemetry fields and alert thresholds.
